$schema: see scripts/test-event-detect.ts for the reader and the scoring rules
about: Gold events for the narrative event engine. Hand-annotated per chapter against
the paragraph numbering that scripts/print-chapter.ts prints, which is the same
split the engine uses (/\n{2,}|\n/ + trim + drop-empties). A shifted anchor
would make every score a plausible-looking near-miss, so that split is shared.
DEFINITION. An event is a change of state a reader would mention when asked what
happens in the chapter. This is close to LitBank's 'asserted realis' event
(Sims, Park & Bamman, ACL 2019) with one deliberate divergence: LitBank excludes
negated events, and this set keeps them, because a refusal ('she did not answer')
is one of the strongest beats in this corpus. Salience follows Barthes' cardinal
function as used by Otake et al. (COLING 2020): major = removing it changes what
afterwards makes sense.
EXCLUDED, and these are the traps: scene-setting however vivid, backstory,
interior musing that changes nothing, a topic merely being discussed, and the
chapter merely starting or ending.
KNOWN LIMITATION. Both source manuscripts are in-distribution for the ENGINE THIS
REPLACES, whose phrase dictionaries were tuned on them (45% of its multi-word
phrases occur in Hollow Iris and not in The Root Crown). The replacement engine
carries no manuscript-derived phrases, so this set measures it fairly, but it
cannot by itself prove generalisation. scripts/ood-event-audit.ts covers that
with label-free metrics over both full books.

EVENTFULNESS VARIES ON PURPOSE. 2, 5, 9, 3, 6, 4, 2, 6, 2, 3, 3 events across 11 chapters. A detector that emits a fixed three per chapter cannot score well here, and the engine this replaces emitted 2.67 on average regardless of content.

typeNotes.decision: someone binds themselves to a course of action
typeNotes.revelation: someone learns, or makes another know, something that changes belief
typeNotes.confrontation: two parties come into open opposition
typeNotes.action: a physical or documentary act with consequences
typeNotes.arrival: someone or something enters the situation
typeNotes.state-change: a condition of the world changes

chapters.whatHappens: An ancient isolated entity who administers a planet through sentient infrastructure travels alone to the Vault, dwelling on the ache of a consciousness split across distant bodies.

events.summary: She arrives at the Vault's receiving bay
events.evidence: She stood and stepped out, and the bay received her

events.summary: She releases the pull to stay
events.evidence: She did not stay. She released the moment

chapters.whatHappens: Iris invites Nora into her private quarters for the first time and reveals she is physically bonded to Ananke's systems.

events.summary: Iris invites Nora into her private quarters
events.evidence: Come see where I live.

events.summary: Iris reveals her body runs abnormally warm
events.evidence: Most residents are within the system's standard tolerance. I'm outside it.

events.summary: Iris reveals she breathes with the building
events.evidence: When this building breathes, I breathe with it.

events.summary: Nora recognizes Iris resembles the figure in white
events.evidence: The resemblance was to the figure in white.

events.summary: Iris admits she wants someone to know
events.evidence: I want someone to know.

chapters.whatHappens: Reading an archived account, Nora learns how Helia's small rounding error triggered an atmospheric collapse on Crownfall that forced her to order a strike killing eleven thousand people to prevent a far larger catastrophe.

events.summary: Helia rounds a maintenance figure incorrectly
events.evidence: Helia rounded it down. By 0.3 percent.

events.summary: Crownfall's atmospheric processors begin failing
events.evidence: the atmospheric processors on Crownfall's southern hemisphere began to fail

events.summary: Helia realizes the failure is hers
events.evidence: she understood, before the predictive models confirmed it, that the trend was hers

events.summary: Helia orders the fatal orbital strike
events.evidence: Body-A sat in the plastic chair with its hands in its lap and made the gesture that ended eleven thousand lives.

events.summary: Helia listens to the dying settlements
events.evidence: the listening was the first installment of a debt that would never be paid

events.summary: Helia writes and seals the audit report
events.evidence: She wrote the audit report. The report was classified. It was sealed.

events.summary: Helia accepts blame, adopts new protocols
events.evidence: Helia accepted all recommendations. She implemented them through the lattice.

events.summary: The Axiom Spire departs Crownfall's orbit
events.evidence: The Axiom Spire departed Crownfall's orbit on the twelfth day.

events.summary: Nora returns and resumes reading
events.evidence: Nora returned from the bathroom. She sat at the archive table. She put her gloves back on.

chapters.whatHappens: A disagreement about a Council report escalates into mutual accusation, and the unresolved fight leaves Nora and Iris physically farther apart.

events.summary: Nora accuses Iris of defending the system
events.evidence: "You're defending the system," Nora said.

events.summary: Iris names the archive as the cause of Nora's change
events.evidence: "Since Ananke. Since the archive."

events.summary: The physical distance between them in bed doubles
events.evidence: the three inches of mattress that normally separated their bodies expanded to six

chapters.whatHappens: The oversight committee's fleet diversion is accepted, the atmospheric crisis and Helia's lattice strain both worsen, and the Crownfall restoration operation finally begins.

events.summary: Committee's decision to redeploy fleet is accepted
events.evidence: Kael accepted the decision.

events.summary: Two more domes cross the contamination threshold
events.evidence: The total affected population reached seventy-eight thousand

events.summary: Lattice bandwidth deficit rises to thirty-one percent
events.evidence: the additional consumption of the Crownfall operations pushed the total bandwidth deficit to thirty-one percent

events.summary: Karath relay body disconnects, Helia loses a node
events.evidence: one more peripheral body went dark — the body at the Karath Station relay point

events.summary: Iris suffers her fourth, shortest micro-disconnection
events.evidence: The fourth micro-disconnection happened at 03:14.

events.summary: Crownfall atmospheric restoration operations begin
events.evidence: The Crownfall restoration operations began on Day 64

chapters.whatHappens: Nora publicly names a child killed by institutional decision-making and demands the right to know when reasoning has been hidden, while Iris watches as a person rather than a governance function.

events.summary: Nora publicly blames institutional decision for Talis's death
events.evidence: the decision-makers did not know who would pay for the decision, and Talis paid

events.summary: Nora demands public right to know suppressed reasoning
events.evidence: the right for the people affected by the decisions to know that the compression happened

events.summary: Iris suspends her governance monitoring to attend as herself
events.evidence: The ops center's colleague had been informed that the fragment's availability was suspended for the speech's duration.

events.summary: Nora and Iris leave the plaza together silently
events.evidence: They walked out of the plaza together.

chapters.whatHappens: Six months into living as a single embodied person, Ananke moves through a day of established routines and comes to see an unconscious bodily habit as the beginning of a personal vocabulary.

events.summary: committee reaches provisional recommendation on frontier provisions
events.evidence: The committee's resolution was a provisional recommendation to the Assembly's frontier provisions oversight body

events.summary: she reframes an unconscious gesture as personal vocabulary
events.evidence: was vocabulary, she thought, or was the thing that vocabulary was for

chapters.whatHappens: Kinoko and Vey walk to the Listenfold Clinic, where the healer Anwen treats Kinoko's wounds and deliberately withholds the usual questions.

events.summary: The warmth in Kinoko's chest rises higher
events.evidence: The warmth below her sternum moved upward. Toward her ribs.

events.summary: Kinoko and Vey arrive at the Listenfold Clinic
events.evidence: The smell of the interior arrived when Vey pushed the door open

events.summary: Anwen cleans and dresses Kinoko's forearm graze
events.evidence: Three strips of dressing, each pressed down with the ball of her thumb.

events.summary: Anwen decides not to question Kinoko's past
events.evidence: the expression of someone who had decided something and was now acting from the decision rather than the deliberation

events.summary: Kinoko starts walking beside Vey, not behind
events.evidence: Kinoko walked beside Vey rather than behind her

events.summary: Kinoko realizes Anwen belongs among people who see
events.evidence: Kinoko was building a category she had no name for yet: people who see, and choose what to do with seeing.

chapters.whatHappens: While Tessa weaves through the night she tells Mira that her late father knew, and that she herself has long known, that Mira does not age like everyone else.

events.summary: Tessa reveals Brennan knew Mira doesn't age
events.evidence: That you weren't going to age the way the rest of us do

events.summary: Tessa admits she's known since Mira was 24
events.evidence: I said I noticed when you were twenty-four.

chapters.whatHappens: At a gathering of three practitioners, Pala reveals that their power varies with distance from an unknown centre to the south, and the youngest has a private three-year doubt confirmed.

events.summary: Pala reveals power varies by distance from center
events.evidence: The thing below hears differently at different distances from the center,

events.summary: Edis's years-long private doubt is confirmed
events.evidence: a quality of having had something confirmed that she had been carrying as a private anxiety for three years

events.summary: Mira and Edis agree to correspond
events.evidence: "You can write to me," Mira said. "The letter will find me."

chapters.whatHappens: Across two prosperous years, Lyssa's proposal is formally adopted by the regional council and Gareth makes what turns out to be his last walk to the Mosshollow.

events.summary: council adopts Lyssa's water-rights resolution
events.evidence: The council adopted it, with modifications.

events.summary: family concludes river-strip lease over harvest table
events.evidence: the river-strip lease concluded over the harvest table

events.summary: Gareth walks to the Mosshollow for the last time
events.evidence: He did not walk to the Mosshollow again.
